ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mystic botany
ResearchProjectDef.description: Wild mystic flowers grow across the rim. Learning which ones hold mana, and how to plant them again, is where every Botania colony starts.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana
ResearchProjectDef.description: Study how certain flowers hold energy in their petals, and build the petal apothecary that turns them into something usable.\n\nThis is the root of the whole line. Once it is done the tree forks three ways: flowers that make mana, flowers that spend it on work, and flowers that fight. Grinding petals also yields mana powder, which can be folded into steel or bound into wood, and stored in a pool of liquid light.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: garden craft
ResearchProjectDef.description: Bind livingwood and livingrock into a staff that can channel mana. This is where the wand of the forest is built, and where the colony learns to shape living materials instead of only cutting them.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: manasteel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Fold mana powder into steel to make manasteel: light, tough, and the skeleton of every advanced mana structure, from pools and relays to fluxfields and repairers.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana storage
ResearchProjectDef.description: Manasteel can hold far more mana than livingrock. A proper manasteel-lined pool keeps a colony's whole reserve in one place instead of spilling it across a dozen small bowls.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana infusion
ResearchProjectDef.description: An infusion table that lets a colony craft high-tier goods out of mana instead of electricity.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: mana grid
ResearchProjectDef.description: Rope the colony's mana into one grid: relays with longer reach and bigger pools, so a dozen scattered flowers can feed a single reserve.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: wand forms
ResearchProjectDef.description: Reforge the wand of the forest into two specialised forms. The sniper form trades rate of fire for one dense lance that punches through armour. The blast form throws slow, unstable bolts that burst into a cross of fire wherever they land, friend or foe. Neither form keeps the wand's plant-magic.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: alfheim gate
ResearchProjectDef.description: A gate frame that trades mana for elven materials. It only works with a lintel and both pillars standing: leave livingwood, livingrock or petals in the doorway and it draws mana from a nearby pool to turn them into dreamwood, elven quartz, pixie dust and elementium ingot.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: elementium
ResearchProjectDef.description: Elementium is the pink metal the elven gate makes from manasteel and pixie dust: it bends instead of shattering, and it keeps an edge that steel loses after a single fight.\n\nThis project is the kit built from it: a spacer-grade sword, a full suit of plate (1.04 sharp / 0.42 blunt / 0.49 heat) with a matching helm at 60% of the body rating, and the pixie lamp, which burns dust for a soft permanent glow. Elementium sits between manasteel and terrasteel - better than anything the colony can forge itself, short of what the gaia spirit teaches.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: terrasteel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Feed manasteel and elven quartz to a ring of four pedestals and draw twenty thousand mana through it. What comes out is terrasteel: metal that grows. Every piece of it buys one blade, one suit of plate or one helm.

ResearchProjectDef.label: botania: gaia
ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: unlocked by a gaia spirit techprint, not by points alone. Content arrives in a later version.
